monitor: It can also mean to watch or observe something carefully.
It is commonly found on a desk.
It displays information from a computer.
It is a separate screen commonly used with desktop computers.
mouse: It is also the name of a small animal.
You move it around to control something on a screen.
It usually has buttons and a scroll wheel.
You use it to point, click, and select things on a computer.
laptop: Its name describes something you could use while sitting on your lap.
It is a portable type of computer.
It has a built-in screen and keyboard.
You can carry it around and use it without staying at a desk.
usb: Its full name contains the word 'bus,' but it has nothing to do with transportation.
It is commonly used to connect devices and transfer data.
You may plug a cable or flash drive into it.
USB ports and cables are commonly used with computers and phones.
browser: It describes something used to explore or look through information.
It is software used to access the web.
You use it to visit websites and search online.
Chrome, Firefox, and Edge are examples of this.
website: The word combines 'web' with a place or location.
It is something you visit using the internet.
It can contain pages, images, videos, and information.
You open one by entering its address or clicking a link.
cloud: It is normally associated with the sky, but technology uses it differently.
It allows information to be stored somewhere other than your device.
You can access your files through the internet.
Online services use this to store and access data remotely.
server: In everyday language, this word can describe someone who serves people.
In technology, it provides information or services to other computers.
Websites and apps often depend on one of these.
It receives requests and sends data back to connected devices.
database: It combines something that means facts with something that stores them.
It organizes large amounts of information.
Websites and applications often use one to store user information.
It can contain tables, records, and other structured data.
data: It comes from a Latin word meaning 'things given.'
Computers process this to produce useful information.
Photos, numbers, messages, and documents can all be examples of it.
It is one of the most basic things stored and processed by computers.
file: It can also describe a collection of papers kept together.
Computers use it to store information.
Photos, documents, and videos can all be examples of this.
You can save, copy, rename, move, or delete one on a computer.
folder: It normally describes something used to organize papers.
Computers use it to organize files.
You can put documents, photos, and other files inside one.
It helps keep your computer files organized.
memory: It can describe the ability to remember something.
Computers also need this to work with information.
RAM is a type of this used by computers.
It temporarily holds information that programs are actively using.
storage: It describes keeping something for future use.
Technology uses it to keep digital information.
Files, photos, and videos take up this on your devices.
Hard drives, SSDs, and cloud services can provide this.
processor: It describes something that processes or handles something.
It is one of the most important parts inside a computer.
It is often called the CPU or the 'brain' of a computer.
software: It refers to something that is not a physical object.
Computers need it to perform specific tasks.
Apps and programs are types of this.
It is the set of programs and instructions that run on a device.
hardware: It refers to something physical rather than something purely digital.
Computers are made from many different parts of this type.
A keyboard, mouse, and processor are examples.
It refers to the physical components of a computer or device.
code: It can mean a system of symbols or instructions.
Computers use it to understand what they should do.
Programmers write this using programming languages.
It is the written instructions behind many apps and websites.
programming: It describes the act of creating instructions.
It involves telling computers how to perform tasks.
People do this using languages such as Python, Java, or C++.
It is the process of writing and organizing computer code.
algorithm: It describes a method for solving a problem.
It usually involves a sequence of steps.
Computers use these to process information and make decisions.
A recipe-like set of instructions for solving a problem is an example.
app: It is a shortened form of a longer technology word.
You probably use several of these every day.
You can download them from an app store.
Games, social media, and messaging programs on phones are examples.
icon: It can also describe a famous or important person.
In technology, it is usually a small visual symbol.
You often see these on your phone or computer screen.
Tapping or clicking one can open an app or perform an action.
notification: It means information given to make someone aware of something.
Your devices can show these when something happens.
Messages and app updates can trigger one.
It often appears as a pop-up, sound, or small alert on your phone.
cable: It refers to something used to connect two points.
Technology uses many different types of these.
They can carry power, data, or signals.
USB, HDMI, and Ethernet are common examples.
adapter: It describes something that makes two different things work together.
You may need one when connectors or plugs do not match.
Phones and laptops often use these with chargers and ports.
It can convert or connect one type of connection to another.
router: It normally describes something that directs a route.
It helps devices communicate across a network.
Many homes have one that provides wireless internet.
It sends network traffic between your devices and the internet.
network: It describes a group of connected things.
Computers and devices can form one to communicate.
Wi-Fi is one way devices can connect to one.
It allows devices to communicate and share information.
signal: It can mean a sign that communicates information.
Phones and wireless devices rely on this.
You may check its strength when your connection is poor.
The bars on your phone often indicate the strength of this.
screen: It can also mean to filter or evaluate something.
You look at one when using many electronic devices.
Phones, computers, and televisions commonly have one.
It displays the images and information you interact with.
touchscreen: It combines an action with something you look at.
You interact with it directly using your fingers.
Phones and tablets commonly use this technology.
Tapping and swiping the display are ways of using it.
camera: It originally referred to a room or chamber.
It is used to capture moments visually.
It can take photographs and record videos.
Phones, laptops, and standalone devices can all have one.
speaker: It can also describe someone giving a speech.
Technology uses it to produce sound.
You can connect one to a phone or computer to hear audio.
It turns an electrical or digital signal into sound you can hear.
microphone: People often shorten this word to three letters.
You might use one during a presentation or video call.
It is the device that picks up your voice for recording or communication.
webcam: It combines the web with something used to capture images.
It is commonly built into laptops.
It lets people see you during an online meeting.
It is a camera designed for computers and online video.
selfie: It describes a picture taken by the person in the picture.
Phones made this type of photo extremely common.
People usually use the front-facing camera for one.
It is a self-taken photo, often shared online.
video: It comes from Latin and is connected with seeing.
It is one of the most common forms of digital media.
It combines moving images, usually with sound.
YouTube, TikTok, and streaming services contain millions of these.
streaming: It originally relates to something flowing continuously.
Technology uses it for media delivered over the internet.
You can watch movies or listen to music this way.
Instead of downloading the entire file first, you receive the media as it plays.
social: It relates to interaction between people.
Technology has made this a major part of online communication.
It is commonly paired with the word 'media.'
Platforms where people post, share, follow, and comment are called this type of media.
email: It is a shortened form of 'electronic mail.'
It is one of the oldest common forms of digital communication.
You can send messages and attach files using it.
Messages sent through Gmail or Outlook are examples.
password: It is something you normally keep private.
It helps protect access to an account.
You enter it when logging into many websites and applications.
username: It combines a person who uses something with a name.
It identifies you when using many online services.
It is often entered together with a password.
It is the name or ID you use to log into an account.
login: It describes entering a system rather than physically entering a building.
You do this when accessing a protected account.
It usually requires a username and password.
You do this before accessing many websites and apps.
security: It is about keeping something safe from danger or unwanted access.
It is especially important when using the internet.
Passwords and authentication help provide it.
It protects devices, accounts, networks, and information.
privacy: It describes keeping certain information away from others.
It is an important concern when using websites and apps.
Personal information can be protected by it.
It concerns who can see or use your personal information.
virus: It is also used in biology.
In computers, it refers to harmful software.
It can spread between files or devices.
Antivirus software can detect and remove this type of threat.
backup: It means keeping something as protection in case the original is lost.
It is important for protecting digital files.
You can make a copy of your photos and documents this way.
A backup lets you restore information after losing the original.
update: It means bringing something to a newer or more current state.
Your devices may ask you to do this regularly.
Apps and operating systems receive these to improve or fix things.
Installing a newer version of software is an example.
download: The word describes moving something downward.
You do this when getting a file from the internet.
Photos, apps, videos, and documents can all be transferred this way.
It means moving digital information from the internet onto your device.
upload: You do this when sending a file to an online service.
Posting a photo or video can involve this process.
It means transferring a file from your device to the internet or a server.
printer: It once described a person's profession.
It turns digital information into something physical.
It usually works with paper and ink or toner.
It produces physical copies of documents and images.
scanner: It describes something that examines or reads something carefully.
It can turn physical documents into digital files.
You place a paper document on one to capture it.
It is commonly used to digitize documents and images.
remote: It means something that is far away.
Technology uses it to control devices from a distance.
You might use one while sitting on a couch.
A television controller is commonly called a remote.
controller: It describes something used to control another thing.
It usually has buttons and sometimes sticks.
It lets you control characters and actions in video games.
console: It can also describe a type of control panel.
Many people associate it with gaming.
It connects to a television or monitor for playing games.
PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch are examples.
pixel: Its name comes from combining two words related to pictures.
It is one of the tiny building blocks of a digital image.
Screens are made up of millions of these.
More of these can help create higher-resolution images.
resolution: It can also mean a decision made after considering a problem.
In technology, it describes how much visual detail something can show.
It is commonly associated with screens and images.
1080p and 4K are examples of display resolutions.
bluetooth: Its unusual name comes from a historical figure.
It allows nearby devices to communicate wirelessly.
Headphones, speakers, keyboards, and phones commonly use it.
You often 'pair' devices when connecting them with this technology.
qr: Its name is an abbreviation involving the word 'quick.'
It is made from a pattern of small squares.
You usually scan it with a phone camera.
Scanning one can open a website, menu, form, or other information.
barcode: This technology uses a visual pattern to represent information.
You often see one on products in stores.
A scanner reads it to identify an item.
The lines and numbers on a product label form one.
gps: Its name is an abbreviation for a system that helps determine position.
Phones and cars commonly use it.
It helps you figure out where you are and where to go.
It uses satellites to provide location and navigation information.
smartphone: It combines an everyday device with the idea of intelligence.
It is more than just a device for making calls.
It can run apps, browse the internet, and take photos.
Modern phones such as iPhones and Android devices are examples.
tablet: It can also describe a small pill or an ancient writing surface.
Most modern versions are controlled by touching the screen.
It is larger than a phone but usually smaller than a laptop.
An iPad is a famous example of this type of device.
battery: It is also used for a group of guns or a series of tests.
It stores energy so a device can run without being plugged in.
It comes in sizes like AA and AAA, and some types are rechargeable.
Your phone or laptop shuts down when this runs out.
computer: It once described a person who did calculations by hand.
It follows instructions written as code.
It has a processor, memory, and storage.
It can be a desktop or a laptop, and you are probably using one right now.
headphones: It is plural because there are two of them, one for each side.
They are worn over or in your ears.
They let you listen to audio without other people hearing it.
They connect with a cable or over Bluetooth, and some have a built-in microphone.
internet: It combines a prefix meaning 'between' with the word 'network'.
It connects billions of devices around the world.
It is how websites, emails, and streaming videos reach you.
You need a router or a mobile data plan to get onto it.
keyboard: It is also used for the part of a piano that you press with your fingers.
It has letters, numbers, and function keys.
It is how you type text into a computer.
The most common layout is named after the first six letters on its top row.
phone: It is short for a longer word that comes from Greek for 'sound' or 'voice'.
People used to attach one to a wall with a curly cord.
You use it to call and text other people.
Today most people carry one in their pocket, with a touchscreen and apps.
robot: It comes from a Czech word meaning 'forced labor'.
It is a machine that can follow programmed instructions.
Factories use them to assemble cars and other products.
In movies, it is often a metal machine that looks or acts like a person.
wifi: It is a brand name that people often mistake for an abbreviation.
It sends data through the air using radio waves.
Cafes and airports often offer it for free, sometimes with a password.
It connects your devices to a router without any cables.
bandwidth: It describes how much information can travel through a connection at one time.
It is often measured in bits per second.
Streaming video and large downloads can use a lot of it.
It represents the maximum capacity of a network connection.
cache: It can describe a place where supplies are kept for later use.
Computers store recently used information in it.
It helps pages and programs load more quickly.
It is temporary storage that reduces the need to fetch the same data again.
compiler: It combines two parts of the word 'computer.'
It translates program instructions into a form a computer can run.
It checks the code and produces an executable program.
It turns source code into machine instructions.
debugger: It starts with a word that means to remove insects.
Programmers use it to find and fix problems in code.
It lets you pause a program and inspect what is happening.
It is a tool used to investigate errors during software development.
encryption: It begins with a word that means to hide or cover something.
It turns readable information into a coded form.
It helps keep private messages and transactions secure.
It uses a key so only authorized people can read the original information.
firewall: A wall of a building can stop fire from spreading.
A network uses something similar to block unwanted traffic.
It helps protect computers and private networks.
It is a security system that controls connections between devices.
antivirus: It starts with a prefix meaning 'against.'
It is software designed to find and remove harmful programs.
It helps protect computers from malware.
It scans files and activity for threats to keep a device safe.
framework: It describes a supporting structure that something is built on.
Developers use it to build software more efficiently.
It provides reusable tools and organized rules.
It is a foundation that simplifies the creation of applications.
bytecode: It is made from a basic unit of computer information and a word for code.
It is an intermediate form of instructions.
A virtual machine can run it on different computer systems.
Compilers and virtual machines use it to execute programs.
codec: It combines two parts of words for coding and decoding.
It converts media so it takes less space or transmits smoothly.
Video and audio players rely on it.
It is a tool or format for compressing and decompressing digital media.
malware: It combines a prefix meaning bad with a type of software.
It is made to damage systems, steal information, or cause harm.
Antivirus software and careful downloads help protect against it.
It is a general term for harmful software such as viruses and spyware.
latency: It describes a delay between sending something and receiving a response.
It can be noticeable during online calls or action games.
Network conditions affect how much of it there is.
It is the waiting time between a request and the device answering it.
protocol: It is also used in science and medicine for a set of agreed rules.
Computers use one so devices can communicate in an agreed way.
Web pages rely on rules for requesting and sending information.
It is a defined set of rules that lets computer systems exchange data.
directory: It describes a place where many items are kept in an organized structure.
Computers use it to group files and other locations.
It can contain files or links to other areas of storage.
It is a structured location in a file system that holds files or other folders.
metadata: It is made from a word for information and a word for data.
It describes information about other information rather than the main content.
Files, photos, and websites all contain it.
It includes details such as a file's type, size, date, author, or location.
binary: It means involving two parts or two possible values.
Digital computers use a base-two system to represent data.
Its digits are often written as zero and one.
It describes data represented using a two-state system.
javascript: It is made from a popular programming language name followed by a word describing written code.
Web pages use it to react to clicks and change what users see.
It runs in many browsers and can also run on servers.
It is a high-level programming language commonly used for interactive web pages.
firmware: This is software stored permanently on a device rather than installed normally.
It controls basic hardware functions when the device starts.
Updates to it can improve how a device behaves.
It is low-level software that controls hardware without needing an operating system.
middleware: This word describes software that sits between two other programs.
It helps separate systems communicate and share services.
It can provide connections, security, or common functions.
It is software that connects applications and systems to one another.
hyperlink: This word combines a prefix meaning beyond with a word for a link.
Clicking it takes you to another place in a document or on the web.
Web pages use it to connect related pages.
It is a clickable reference that opens another document or location.
clipboard: This word names an object that temporarily holds copied information.
Computers let you paste from it into another place.
It can contain text, images, or other content.
It is a temporary storage area for content copied or cut from a device.
spreadsheet: This word combines a word for a sheet with a word describing spread-out information.
It organizes information in rows and columns.
It is useful for calculations, records, and budgets.
It is a document or program used to store and calculate tabular data.
cryptography: This word comes from a Greek word meaning hidden writing.
It studies methods for keeping information private.
It is used in secure communication and digital protection.
It is the science of protecting information through codes and mathematical methods.
boot: Computers use it to load the basic software that starts the system.
The startup process is sometimes called this.
It is the process of starting a computer and loading its essential software.
wireless: This word describes a connection that does not use a cable.
It commonly sends information through radio waves.
Phones and computers use it to connect to networks.
It means communicating without a physical cable between devices.
toolbar: This word combines a word for a tool with a word for a bar.
It contains buttons for common commands.
Editors and design programs often place it near the top.
It is a strip of controls used to access tools quickly.
workspace: This word combines a word for work with a word for a place.
It is an area where a person works or stores project files.
Programming tools can organize a project inside one.
It is a designated area used for tasks, files, and project settings.
interface: This word describes the point where a person or system meets another system.
Users interact with software through one.
It connects hardware and software components.
It is a boundary that lets users or systems interact with a computer program or device.
semaphore: This word originally refers to a signaling device using flags.
Computers use a related idea to control access to shared resources.
It helps prevent tasks from conflicting with one another.
It is a synchronization mechanism that controls access using signals or shared values.
iterator: This word comes from a familiar word about repeatedly visiting places.
Programming uses it to move through a collection one item at a time.
It helps loops and data structures process items.
It is an object or mechanism that provides sequential access to a sequence of values.
